challenge.name: Total Recall
challenge.description: Can you recall how to get out of this one? Binary: https://sunshinectf.games/files/54cf6a/total_recall

records.findings_summary: Flag found via SROP (sigreturn-oriented programming) exploit against a tiny static x86-64 binary that only uses raw syscalls. The program leaks 8 bytes of the stack pointer (write(1,rsp,8)), then does read(0,rsp-0x40,0x18), then read(0,rsp-0x80,0x400) which overflows a 128-byte stack buffer. The stack is NX so ret2shellcode fails. Using the stack leak, overwrite the saved return address to re-enter the reading routine; read() return value lands in rax. Sending exactly 15 bytes on the second read makes rax=15 (rt_sigreturn), then return to the syscall;ret gadget at 0x401069 so the kernel performs rt_sigreturn, restoring a staged SigreturnFrame with rax=59 (execve), rdi=pointer to /bin/sh on the stack, rsi=0, rdx=0, rip=syscall gadget, yielding a shell.: sun{r3caLl_ev3Ry_reGist3r_sR0p} | Evidence: Disassembly: 0x401016 leaks stack via write(1,rsp,8); 0x40104f does read(0,rsp-0x80,0x400) = stack overflow; /proc/pid/maps shows stack is rw-p (NX). ; Gadgets: syscall;ret at 0x401069, ret at 0x40104e, read-func entry at 0x40104f. ; Two-stage SROP: first big read stages SigreturnFrame at leaked stack address; second read of exactly 15 bytes makes read() return 15 so rax=15 = rt_sigreturn. ; Local reproduction with setarch -R produced a root shell (PWNED_MARKER_42). ; Remote run gave uid=1337(total_recall) shell and printed flag: sun{r3caLl_ev3Ry_reGist3r_sR0p}.
solution_steps: Download binary from https://sunshinectf.games/files/54cf6a/total_recall; it is static, stripped, syscall-only.
Disassembly shows write(1,rsp,8) leak at 0x401016, and an overflow read(0,rsp-0x80,0x400) at 0x40104f into a 128-byte buffer; stack is non-executable.

Overwrite f2 return address with 0x40104f to re-enter the read function, and place a fake SigreturnFrame (rax=59 execve, rdi=stack pointer to /bin/sh, rsi=0, rdx=0, rip=0x401069 syscall;ret) after it.
Second read sends exactly 15 bytes so read() returns 15, setting rax=15 (rt_sigreturn); return to 0x401069 to trigger rt_sigreturn, kernel restores the frame and runs execve(/bin/sh).
Both local (setarch -R) and remote yielded a shell; cat /flag* on remote returned sun{r3caLl_ev3Ry_reGist3r_sR0p}.
evidence: Disassembly: 0x401016 leaks stack via write(1,rsp,8); 0x40104f does read(0,rsp-0x80,0x400) = stack overflow; /proc/pid/maps shows stack is rw-p (NX).
Gadgets: syscall;ret at 0x401069, ret at 0x40104e, read-func entry at 0x40104f.
Two-stage SROP: first big read stages SigreturnFrame at leaked stack address; second read of exactly 15 bytes makes read() return 15 so rax=15 = rt_sigreturn.
Local reproduction with setarch -R produced a root shell (PWNED_MARKER_42).
Remote run gave uid=1337(total_recall) shell and printed flag: sun{r3caLl_ev3Ry_reGist3r_sR0p}.
Platform submission returned CORRECT (page alert Correct).
